skwird for Linux on x86-64, with glibc 2.35 or later
====================================================

skwird is an index of file names kept current by the system's change
notifications, answered over a local socket. Nothing here is set up for
you: what follows is each way to run it, by hand.

On demand
---------

A client (skwir, or skwird's own commands) starts the engine where none
answers, if skwird is on your PATH; it goes a minute after its last
client:

    install -Dm755 skwird ~/.local/bin/skwird

With your session (systemd)
---------------------------

The user service and its socket, the service pointed at where skwird is
(%h is your home, as systemd spells it):

    install -Dm644 systemd/skwird.service systemd/skwird.socket -t ~/.config/systemd/user
    sed -i 's|/usr/bin/skwird|%h/.local/bin/skwird|' ~/.config/systemd/user/skwird.service
    systemctl --user daemon-reload
    systemctl --user enable --now skwird.socket

The system service (systemd, as root)
-------------------------------------

Every user's files indexed, each user answered only what they could
list. It needs its user (sysusers), and skwird where its unit runs it:

    install -Dm755 skwird /usr/bin/skwird
    install -Dm644 systemd/skwird-system.service -t /usr/lib/systemd/system
    install -Dm644 sysusers/skwird.conf -t /usr/lib/sysusers.d
    systemd-sysusers
    systemctl daemon-reload
    systemctl enable --now skwird-system.service

To stop your engine where it runs this copy: skwird stop. skwird --help
says the rest. Its licences are LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE; what it
holds of others', THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.
